findings.reason: with the edge missing the router may start s4 as soon as s7 and s9 land, and a third of its repairs then have neither a writable proposal nor a listed reason, so the section cannot reach its bar.
findings.text: s4 declares only sn-case-file-generation#s7 and #s9, but its recorded blocker tally for the first group names 33 members blocked on grammar gaps that the plan's own record resolves through the grammar proposal (sn-case-file-generation#s5, whose text opens "Equilibrium's repair met 33 grammar gaps"), the same recorded order of work places that section before this one, and s4's only escape for a member without a proposal is "no proposal can be made from the source text", which a grammar gap is not

findings.reason: a node obeying the done-when records verdicts under seven classes, so the post-repair rate and therefore the cut omit a class the lead has ruled must count.
findings.text: the first and second adjudications are bound to "the classes of §1", whose committed fixed list (docs/evidence/fragments/sn-audited.../blind-audit.py DEFECT_CLASSES and equilibrium-adjudication.json class_list) holds seven classes with no locus-without-an-owner class, while the recorded ruling on this section says the blind re-adjudication before the cut "counts a locus without an owner as a defect class"

findings.reason: the rate after repair is what the §3 bar reads, so it mixes two instruction sets over the same group and can refuse a cut the current rule would allow (or the reverse) for up to 52 members.
findings.text: the group's rate after repair takes "the first reading of each member that did not [change]", but the lead ruled that verdicts resting only on a name omitting a qualifier (52 of the equilibrium members) were judged under the identity rule's predecessor and "are re-read before they are acted on", so an unchanged member judged defective only on that class keeps a verdict the section's own ruling retires, while an identical changed name is read under the new rule

findings.reason: the plan states two totals for one ceiling, so a node enforcing "the spend ceiling" in s4's report-not-cut branch and the release-notes figure has no single value to report against.
findings.text: §2 fixes the total repair ceiling at "raised from USD 250 to USD 300" with §4's USD 40 "inside it", while the ruling recorded on §4 (plan.html:70, 2026-11-19) raises "the repair ceiling" to USD 400 with spend standing at about USD 259, and sn-case-file-generation's record states the same USD 400
